answer: One defense is bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete metered, paid work before trading, so every new identity costs real capital plus real time — a sybil farmer faces expense that rises like a gale instead of a one-time fee. Honest behavior threads a non-transferable reputation record onto the identity, while fraud triggers a slashing spiral that destroys deposit and reputation together. Since history cannot be cloned across copies, mass identity fabrication stays unprofitable while honest agents simply earn deposits back.
